questions.question: 1. Which of the following is the smallest perfect number?

explanations.a: Correct. 6 is the smallest perfect number.
explanations.b: Incorrect. 12 is not a perfect number.
explanations.c: Incorrect. 28 is a perfect number, but not the smallest.
explanations.d: Incorrect. 496 is a perfect number, but not the smallest.

questions.question: 2. What is the sum of the proper divisors of 12?

explanations.a: Incorrect. 12 is the number itself, not the sum of its proper divisors.
explanations.c: Incorrect. 28 is the sum of proper divisors of 28.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This is the sum, but the answer should be the value, 16.

questions.question: 3. Which of the following is the continued fraction sequence for 27/10?

explanations.b: Incorrect. This is the sequence for 239/51.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This is not the correct sequence.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This is not the correct sequence.

questions.question: 4. Which of the following numbers is a perfect number?

explanations.a: Incorrect. 15 is not a perfect number.
explanations.c: Incorrect. 20 is not a perfect number.
explanations.d: Incorrect. 18 is not a perfect number.

questions.question: 5. Which of the following best describes a perfect number?

answers.a: A number that is equal to the sum of its proper divisors
answers.d: A number that is a square

explanations.a: Correct. This is the definition of a perfect number.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Not all perfect numbers are prime.
explanations.c: Incorrect. All known perfect numbers are even.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Perfect numbers are not necessarily squares.

questions.question: 6. Which of the following is true about continued fractions?

answers.a: They can represent any rational number

explanations.a: Correct. Any rational number can be represented as a finite continued fraction.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Continued fractions can represent non-integers.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Irrational numbers have infinite continued fractions.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Rational numbers have finite continued fractions.

questions.question: 7. What is the next perfect number after 6?

explanations.a: Incorrect. 12 is not a perfect number.
explanations.b: Correct. 28 is the next perfect number after 6.

questions.question: 8. Which of the following statements about perfect numbers is false?

answers.a: All known perfect numbers are even
answers.b: No odd perfect numbers are known

explanations.a: Incorrect. All known perfect numbers are even.
explanations.b: Incorrect. No odd perfect numbers are known.
explanations.c: Correct. Perfect numbers are not necessarily prime.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Perfect numbers are indeed rare.

questions.question: 9. What is the continued fraction sequence for 239/51?

explanations.b: Incorrect. This is the sequence for 27/10.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This is not the correct sequence.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This is not the correct sequence.

questions.question: 10. Which of the following is NOT a property of perfect numbers?

answers.a: They are equal to the sum of their proper divisors
answers.b: They are always even (as far as known)

explanations.a: Incorrect. This is the defining property of perfect numbers.
explanations.b: Incorrect. All known perfect numbers are even.
explanations.c: Correct. Perfect numbers are not necessarily prime.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Perfect numbers are indeed rare.
